properties.description: MenloSecurity data connector with template version 3.0.0

connectorUiConfig.title: Menlo Security
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: The [Menlo Security](https://www.menlosecurity.com) connector uses the Menlo Security Logs API to ingest Audit, Bandwidth, and Web proxy logs into Microsoft Sentinel. It runs as three timer-triggered Azure Functions, each polling the API every 3 minutes and writing events to custom Log Analytics tables (`MenloAudit_CL`, `MenloBandwidth_CL`, `MenloWeb_CL`).
connectorUiConfig.lastDataReceivedInfoBalloon: If no new data has been received in the last 3 hours, the connector will display 'not connected'. This can be due to API token expiry, rate limiting, or all log-type functions being disabled.

sampleQueries.description: Top 10 users by web events in the last 24 hours
sampleQueries.query:
MenloWeb_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| summarize Events = count() by userid
| top 10 by Events desc

sampleQueries.description: All audit events in the last 7 days
sampleQueries.query:
MenloAudit_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| project TimeGenerated, uid, audit_actions, sub_event_type, name

sampleQueries.description: Top bandwidth consumers in the last 24 hours
sampleQueries.query:
MenloBandwidth_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| summarize TotalBytes = sum(sum_bytes) by userid
| top 10 by TotalBytes desc

| summarize Time = max(TimeGenerated)
| where isnotempty(Time)

customs.name: Azure permissions for connector deployment
customs.description: Deploying the connector's Azure resources (via the **Deploy to Azure** button in the steps below) requires **Owner**, or **Contributor + User Access Administrator**, on the target resource group — the template creates role assignments that grant the Function App's managed identity access to Key Vault, Storage, and the Data Collection Rule (Contributor alone is not sufficient). Creating the custom tables also requires write access to the Log Analytics workspace's resource group.

instructionSteps.description:
Click **Deploy to Azure** below. On the deployment page:
- For **Resource group**, choose **Create new** and name it `MenloSecurityLogs` so all connector resources stay together and can be removed in one step later.
- Enter your **Log Analytics Workspace Resource Group**, then select your **workspace** from the dropdown. Connector resources are deployed automatically in the **same region as the selected workspace** — no manual region matching is required.
- Enter your **Menlo Security API token**.

The template deploys the Function App, Key Vault, Storage Account, Data Collection Endpoint, and Data Collection Rule, and creates the `MenloAudit_CL`, `MenloBandwidth_CL`, and `MenloWeb_CL` custom tables in your Log Analytics workspace.

[![Deploy To Azure](https://aka.ms/deploytoazurebutton)](https://portal.azure.com/#create/Microsoft.Template/uri/https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2FAzure%2FAzure-Sentinel%2Fmaster%2FSolutions%2FMenloSecurity%2FData%2520Connectors%2Fazuredeploy_MenloSecurity_API_FunctionApp.json/createUIDefinitionUri/https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2FAzure%2FAzure-Sentinel%2Fmaster%2FSolutions%2FMenloSecurity%2FData%2520Connectors%2FcreateUiDefinition_MenloSecurity_API_FunctionApp.json)

_To remove the connector later, delete the `MenloSecurityLogs` resource group and the three `Menlo*_CL` custom tables from the workspace._
instructionSteps.title: Step 1 — Deploy the connector infrastructure

instructionSteps.description:
All log-collection functions are **disabled by default**. After deployment, navigate to the Function App in the Azure Portal and enable the log types you want to collect:

1. Open the **Function App** created by this solution (named `menlo-logs-func-<suffix>`).
2. Go to **Configuration** → **Application settings**.
3. For each log type you want to enable, set the corresponding app setting value to `0`:

| Log type | App setting name | Enable value |
|---|---|---|
| Audit logs | `AzureWebJobs.TimerTriggerAuditLogs.Disabled` | `0` |
| Bandwidth logs | `AzureWebJobs.TimerTriggerBandwidthLogs.Disabled` | `0` |
| Web logs | `AzureWebJobs.TimerTriggerWebLogs.Disabled` | `0` |

4. Click **Save**. Each enabled function will begin polling the Menlo Security API on a 3-minute interval.
instructionSteps.title: Step 2 — Enable log collection

instructionSteps.description:
After enabling at least one log type, wait approximately 5–10 minutes for the first data to appear. Verify by running the following queries in Microsoft Sentinel **Logs**:

```kusto
MenloAudit_CL | take 10
MenloBandwidth_CL | take 10
MenloWeb_CL | take 10
```

If no data appears after 15 minutes, check the Function App's **Monitor** tab for invocation errors.
instructionSteps.title: Step 3 — Verify data ingestion

properties.descriptionHtml:
Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

The Menlo Security solution for Microsoft Sentinel ingests Audit, Bandwidth, and Web proxy logs from the Menlo Security cloud platform into custom Log Analytics tables (MenloAudit_CL, MenloBandwidth_CL, MenloWeb_CL) for threat detection, investigation, and response. Logs are collected by three timer-triggered Azure Functions that poll the Menlo Security Log Fetch API and ship events via the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API using a Data Collection Endpoint (DCE) and Data Collection Rule (DCR).

Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:

This solution takes a dependency on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in Preview state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs:

  1. Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API (DCE/DCR)

  2. Azure Functions

Data Connectors: 1

Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel | Learn more about Solutions
